messages:
incident-bot: Autopager v2 fired for service=redwood.prod.embed-canary, alert=canary-p95-latency, incident=PD-1456. paging 3 on-call targets now. details: https://pd.redwood/PD-1456 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: page triggered -> PD-1456 (escalation policy: prod-deploys). Attempt 1 sent to sarah, attempt 2 -> mike, attempt 3 -> oncall.
sarah: acked PD-1456 (sarahl). looking. seeing spike in canary region us-west-2.
sarah: quick check — traffic split 10% canary -> yes. canary instances report p95 ~1.8s, baseline 220ms.
mike: @sarah is this immediately after the 12:40 deploy? I see a canary rollout at 12:39.
sarah: yes. deploy tag=release/2026-03-15b, image=redwood/infer:rc-2026-03-15b.
alan: I see the same spike in logs, also a flurry of small 503s from sidecar at the same timeframe. samples: 
```
[03/15/2026 12:40:12] canary-03 us-west-2 embed req_id=ab12 p95=1.9s status=200
[03/15/2026 12:40:13] canary-07 us-west-2 embed req_id=cd34 p95=2.1s status=200
[03/15/2026 12:40:14] canary-02 us-west-2 sidecar ERR: batch-queue-timeout
```
julia: Pagerduty shows ack, then autopager retried because silence window didn't hold. PD attempted escalation; oncall missed first two. we might have autopager/backoff interactions.
oncall: I'm on the second rotation now, grabbing signal. can we suppress autopager for this incident? it's flapping.
sarah: trying to mute autopager for service=redwood.prod.embed-canary (manual backoff). command: `pd-suppress --incident PD-1456 --duration 30m --reason "ongoing deploy; investigating"`
incident-bot: suppression request received: autopager-backoff=30m for redwood.prod.embed-canary by sarah. note: suppression does not auto-rollback.
mike: thanks. can we divert traffic off canary to baseline until we find root? `routing override` or scale down canary.
alan: quick mitigation: set traffic split to 0% canary. using routerctl: `routerctl update-split embed-service --canary 0 --baseline 100 --env prod`
alan: running it now...
incident-bot: routerctl change accepted. new split: canary=0%.
sarah: metrics improving on p95 for baseline. canary instances still warming but traffic removed. good confirmation this is deploy-related.
julia: PD note: PD-1456 acknowledged and put on hold due to suppression. escalation paused.
mike: next: decide rollback or patch. canary image looks like it introduced a batching micro-optimization that increases queue hold under short bursts. suspect commit 8f2b1 (batch-compat).
alan: agreed. quick repro locally by replaying short burst traffic reproduces queue-timeouts. patch underway to revert batching change.
sarah: coordinate rollback if patch not ready in 20m. prefer not to roll baseline, only canary. since traffic already 0% it's safe to `kubectl delete --force` the canary ReplicaSet.
mike: I can prepare the rollback command. if patch not ready by 12:58 UTC, we'll remove canary.
oncall: PD note: manual suppression expires in 30m; I'll keep an eye. if autopager re-enables we need to escalate to SRE.
alan: patch PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/patches/pull/423 (revert commit 8f2b1). running CI.
sarah: CI green on unit tests, still running canary integration tests.
julia: small ask — can someone add a short PD note about customer impact? ops email will want summary.
sarah: customers impacted: small subset of embed-heavy queries hitting canary routing; estimated 0.7% of traffic during rollout window. higher p95 for embeds only, no increased error rate overall after traffic removed.
mike: drafting initial incident summary: "Canary release rc-2026-03-15b caused transient p95 latency spike for embed route in us-west-2. Autopager retried and entered backoff/suppression loop due to on-call rotations; manual suppression used and traffic diverted from canary. Patch reverting batching change in review. No customer-facing degradation after diversion; monitoring continues."
alan: CI for patch passed integration tests, merging now. once merged we can re-deploy canary with revert and slowly ramp.
sarah: merging now. deploying `rc-2026-03-15b-revert`. deploy command: `kubectl set image deploy/embed-canary embed=redwood/infer:rc-2026-03-15b-revert -n prod`
alan: new canary coming up. healthchecks show p95 ~230ms within 3 minutes.
julia: nice. PD-1456: marking resolved in PD after confirmation? oncall, can you close?
oncall: I'll update and close PD-1456 in 10m after stability window. leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
sarah: filing postmortem draft, assigning owner: alan. will include timeline and autopager config suggestion to prefer exponential backoff + require explicit suppress confirmation when deploy flag present.
mike: add runbook step: when a canary-caused PD toggles, consider immediate 0% split and suppress autopager to avoid noisy escalation.
incident-bot: Incident PD-1456: status=stabilized, suppression=active until 6150006121, traffic=baseline-only.
julia: thanks everyone — nice coordinated blip.
alan: follow-ups: PR for autopager behavior open #789, postmortem draft link: https://docs.redwood/incidents/PD-1456/postmortem
sarah: closing notes: no SLA breach, customer impact minor. closing thread after postmortem published. :white_check_mark:
